column1: # GUNDAM BREAKER 4 (Switch, update 1.12.0): Bandai Namco, Unreal Engine 4.27 (one version 11 pak with the shaders inline in the cooked packages, MallocBinned3), SDK 12.3.2, NVN, CRIWARE.
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) and brought up on the Android port; the shader tables were split with this repository's shader_split.py + the
# decoded inline packages (DM_UE_INLINE_DECODED). Format: key <TAB> value; several values of one key are separated by spaces; comments must be on their own line
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the game's config sets t.MaxFPS=30 and rhi.syncinterval=2, and its engine runs with bUseFixedFrameRate on. The host writes t.MaxFPS 60 and rhi.SyncInterval 1 into
# the console variables (hle_fpslock.c), and UEngine::FixedFrameRate 60 (the same build's host); present interval 1 then comes from the game. DM_FPS_TARGET=30 keeps the game's 30
# Unreal Engine 4.27: nninitStartup reserves a 62 GB engine region and FMallocBinned3 cuts 37 GB of pools out of it. This build's rewriter is older than the engine-wide rules, so the
# FMallocBinned3 constructor entry is cut in patches.py and the region is capped by the game's own argument (game_args); the memory partition is OCTOPATH TRAVELER II's
# plays with a controller, docked (1920x1080); no touch or pointer input
# Unreal Engine 4.27 with no shader code archives: each material's shaders inline in its cooked package (.uexp) and the engine's global shaders in Engine/GlobalShaderCache-SF_GLSL_SWITCH.bin,
# every one an LZ4 block. The pak's blocks are Oodle-compressed: the Android porter decodes them on the device into DM_UE_INLINE_DECODED (the host's Oodle tool mode, DM_OODLE_JOB_EARLY)
